    Pseudo Out-of-Sample Forecasting for Okun State-Space Model

    forecast_okun_ssm.Rd

    This function performs a rolling pseudo out-of-sample forecast for the unemployment rate. It iterates through a series of "vantage points" (dates), recalculates the cyclical GDP gap using available history and external GDP forecasts, and applies estimated SSM parameters to generate a forecast path.

    forecast_okun_ssm(
  params_df,
  date_col = "quarter",
  exog_var_col = "log_gdp",
  forecast_h = 8,
  Y_data_df = Y_okun,
  target_variable = "unemp_rate",
  X_data = X_okun,
  gdp_gap_forecasts_input = gdp_gap_forecasts
)

    Arguments

    params_df

    A dataframe containing estimated parameters for each vintage. Must include natural_rate, beta1, beta2, and beta3.

    date_col

    Character. The name of the date column (default "quarter").

    exog_var_col

    Character. The column name for the exogenous GDP data (default "log_gdp").

    forecast_h

    Integer. The forecast horizon in quarters (default 8).

    Y_data_df

    Dataframe containing observed dependent variable data (unemp_rate).

    target_variable

    Character. The variable to be forecast (default "unemp_rate").

    X_data

    Dataframe containing historical exogenous data (log GDP).

    gdp_gap_forecasts_input

    Dataframe containing external future GDP forecasts used to extend the HP filter and drive the Okun cyclical component.

    Value

    A dataframe (Evaluation Matrix) where:

    • Columns: Represent the "Vantage Point" (the date the forecast was made).

    • Rows: Represent the "Target Date" (the date being forecast).

    • Diagonal: Contains the actual observed values known at that time.

    • Below Diagonal: Contains the \(h\)-step ahead forecasts.

    Details

    The Pseudo-Real-Time Approach: To mimic actual forecasting conditions, the function:

    1. Data Fusing: For each vintage, it combines historical GDP with external forecasts to create a "complete" series known at that vantage point.

    2. Recalibrated Filtering: It runs the HP filter (\(\lambda = 1600\)) on this fused series to derive the GDP gap. This captures how real-time estimates of the cycle change as new data arrives.

    3. Okun Projection: The cyclical impact is calculated as \(X_t \beta\) and added to the latent structural trend (\(\rho_T\)) following a random walk assumption for the forecast horizon.

    See also

    [predict_ssm_path_rw()]
